chapter: Society bands and white New Orleans attitudes
title: Jazz bands at parties, high school and Tulane dances
summary: Band sizes at private parties grew; at Tulane in 1915-19 the finest bands played script dances and he hired Joe Oliver in Storyville.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, uh, going through your early days, could you tell me, uh, you said that, well, the, uh, jazz music was used a lot for parties, for private parties off of big dances of some sort, and it was accepted as big music to have? Yes. And, uh, that...

And there, there were not always big bands. There may be a single piano, or a piano with rhythm, or two or three string instruments, and then it gradually grew into five and then into seven. But that required the larger homes to have a full band. Well, uh...
Say, when you were in high school, your high school was dancing, was it normal to have a jazz band? Oh, yes. What about in college? Well, at Tulane, the... How many years that you were there?

The gymnasium, yeah. I was in Tulane in 1915. I started, but the war broke out in 16, and I left. And I came back in 19, I think, or 18, and started over. But already they were having... When we were seniors in high school, they were having script dances at the Tulane gym on Saturday night for a dollar a couple. They had nothing but a big pool of ice water at one end, no refreshments. But this, what is now used is, I don't think it's... It's next to the Tulane gym on the campus now. Was it... Do you know which building I'm talking about? It was the... It was the... formerly the Tulane gymnasium. It was further... Uptown and downtown. Further towards Broadway. It was Howard Tilton Library, which is right next to it.
Maybe it's on the other side, but... Maybe ROTC building. What do they have in there now? Maybe ROTC.
Are they sleeping quarters now? I really don't know. I doubt they're sleeping quarters now, unless maybe for the offices.

Well, it could be that, but they had always the finest jazz bands in the city available at that time. Joe Oliver was the most popular band of all, and I remember going down into the old district where he was playing in Storyville to hire him to go for those dances. It was from 8 to 12, and that was it, unless they took up a... Pass the hat and got enough money to keep them to one o'clock, and that was the limit.
